newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close down but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close down but off lows.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed lower Tuesday as cautious buyers stayed away although bargain-hunting helped the market recoup some of its early losses.
The blue chip index closed down 17.99 points, or 0.54 percent, at 3,199.08.
"The bourse was nervous and discouraged when the peso was hit by speculation and by forecasts of primary interest rate hikes," said Hans Klingbeil, trader with the Goldman Sachs brokerage in Mexico.
"Bargain hunters stepped in towards the close as stocks had been hit very hard," he added.

A Reuters survey of 10 money market traders showed they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes to rise by an average of 1.41 percentage points, to 29.11 percent, at the primary Cetes (Treasury bill) auction Tuesday evening.
The benchmark 48-hour peso meanwhile closed 3.6 centavos weaker at 7.9400 per dollar.
Analysts said investor interest also flagged for technical reasons and uncertainty over official economic policy criteria for 1997.

"Jitters appeared when the 3,200 point support was broken," said Jaime Fernandez, analyst at the Interacciones brokerage. "Then some panic selling began, but few wanted to buy either, and that can be seen by the thin volume we had."
Volume was 83.8 million shares traded, but that was inflated by cross trades, especially in holding company Moderna which closed down 15 centavos (2 cents) at 36.00 pesos ($4.53).
On the broad market scoreboard, a total of 104 stocks were traded, of which losers outnumbered gainers by 62 to 26.

Financial stock GFInver LCP series led the gainers list, up eight centavos (1 cent) at 70 centavos (9 cents), in what traders said was a technical rebound after it had been hit severely in the wake of a takeover last week.

Debt-ridden holding company Sidek led the losers, closely followed by its sister companies, steelmakers Simec and tourist operator Situr. The three closed down 11 centavos (1 cent), 26 centavos (3 cents) and 21 centavos (3 cents), respectively, at 94 centavos (12 cents), 1.30 pesos (16 cents) and 1.29 pesos (16 cents).
Traders said the three were hit by Sidek posting net nine-month losses on Monday, and by a judge ruling against the firm in a lawsuit the same day.
